candidats.titre: File:NY Marble Cemetery wall with vault tablets.jpg
candidats.description: The New York Marble Cemetery, with its entrance at 41 Second Avenue between 2nd and 3rd Streets in the East Village neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, was founded in 1830 and was the first non-sectarian cemetery in the city. (Source: Guide to NYC Landmarks (4th ed.)) The Cemetery is generally open to the public on the fourth Sunay of the month from April to October, and on other days throughout the year. (Source: New York Marble Cemetary website ) This picture was taken on May 1, 2011.

candidats.titre: File:Dolomitized marble in marble (Gouverneur Marble, Mesoproterozoic, ~1.1 Ga; Route 11 roadcut north of Antwerp, New York State, USA) 6.jpg
candidats.description: Marble & dolomitized marble in the Precambrian of New York State, USA. Marble is a crystalline-textured metamorphic rock composed of calcite (CaCO3 - calcium carbonate). It bubbles in acid and does not scratch glass. Marble forms by the metamorphism of limestone, a common biogenic sedimentary rock. The outcrop seen here is composed of whitish marble that is graphitic and phlogopitic. Some incorporated calc-silicate rock clasts having reaction rims are present.
